opts: Placenta previa, a previous caesarean, curettage or myomectomy; the cause is defective decidua with absent Nitabuch's layer
Multiparity alone, through an excessively thick and vascular decidua basalis
A twin pregnancy alone, through an unusually thick Nitabuch layer
Maternal anaemia alone, through a hyperplastic and overactive endometrium
exp: Accreta spectrum follows endometrial damage: previa, scar, curettage or myomectomy, with loss of the Nitabuch layer and decidua basalis.

q: Types of lock — English lock (most common) : sliding lock.
opts: English: two sockets, with the left blade introduced first — sliding: one socket that lets the blades slide
English: a single socket — sliding: two sockets with the right blade introduced first
English: a screw mechanism — sliding: a pivot joint between the two shanks
English: no lock at all — sliding: a ratchet that locks at fixed intervals
exp: The English lock has a socket on each handle and closes only when the left blade goes in first; the sliding lock corrects asynclitism.

opts: Measure the uterocervical length, confirm the uterine position and act as the first dilator
Evacuate the products of conception by suction through the cervical canal
Hold and steady the cervix while the suction cannula is introduced
Test the maternal Rh status before any trophoblastic tissue is aspirated
exp: The sound establishes length and axis before instrumentation begins and begins the dilatation; it never aspirates or holds the cervix.

opts: Straight rather than curved, and sited about 3 cm below the line joining the anterior superior iliac spines
Curved rather than straight, and sited lower down close to the symphysis pubis
A vertical midline incision carried down from the umbilicus
A transverse incision placed at the level of the umbilicus
exp: Joel-Cohen is a straight, higher transverse incision with blunt dissection; Pfannenstiel is curved and lower with more dissection.

opts: Chorionicity: monochorionic twins fare worse than dichorionic twins in every outcome
Zygosity alone, since monozygotic twins do badly whatever the placentation
Fetal sex, since unlike-sex twins have the worst perinatal outcome
Maternal parity, since a first twin pregnancy carries the poorest outlook
exp: Chorionicity determines prognosis because it decides whether the circulations are shared; zygosity and sex do not.

opts: The lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh, which is the nerve most often injured
The femoral nerve, compressed against the pelvic brim by the fetal head
The common peroneal nerve, compressed at the neck of the fibula
The obturator nerve, stretched by the descending head in the cavity
exp: Meralgia paraesthetica is entrapment of the lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh under the inguinal ligament in labour.

q: Match FIGO stage to site in gestational trophoblastic neoplasia: stage 2 and stage 4 correspond to:
opts: Stage 2: disease in the pelvis and vagina — stage 4: brain or liver metastasis
Stage 2: disease confined to the uterine corpus — stage 4: pulmonary metastasis
Stage 2: pulmonary metastasis — stage 4: pelvic and vaginal disease
Stage 2: cerebral metastasis — stage 4: disease still confined to the uterus
exp: Stage 1 is confined to the uterus, stage 2 spreads to pelvis and vagina, stage 3 to lung, and stage 4 to brain, liver or kidney.

opts: Placenta previa, abruptio placentae, placenta accreta spectrum and chorioamnionitis
A succenturiate lobe alone, which does not disturb the third stage
A velamentous cord insertion alone, which affects only the fetus
A circumvallate placenta alone, which is a harmless anatomical variant
exp: Placental causes of PPH are previa, abruption, morbid adherence and infection; the others are variants that do not themselves provoke bleeding.

opts: Its tocolytic effect appears only at 9-10 mg/dL, the same range as its toxicity
It causes persistent fetal tachycardia that masks the signs of fetal distress
It has no effect at all on the myometrium at any dose that can be given
It paradoxically induces labour by increasing local prostaglandin release
exp: Magnesium relaxes myometrium only at levels that are already toxic, so it is used for neuroprotection rather than tocolysis.

opts: Previous caesarean, uterine surgery or curettage, and smoking with endometritis
Polyhydramnios, which stretches the uterus and thins the decidua
Folic acid deficiency, which impairs the development of the decidua
Primigravidity, since a first pregnancy leaves behind the most adhesions
exp: Anything that scars or inflames the endometrium prevents the placenta from migrating away from the lower segment.

opts: Her clothes are soaked and she reports a sudden gush followed by continued leaking
Painless bright-red bleeding with a soft and non-tender uterus
Fever with a rigid tender uterus and offensive-smelling lochia
Reduced fetal movements alone, without any loss of fluid or bleeding
exp: Rupture of membranes presents as a sudden gush with continuing leak; bleeding suggests abruption or previa, and fever suggests infection.

opts: Within 3 hours; 1 g in 100 mL of normal saline given intravenously over 20 minutes
Within 24 hours; 500 mg given by intramuscular injection
Within 1 hour; 2 g given as a rapid intravenous bolus
At any time after the bleed; 1 g given orally as a single dose
exp: Tranexamic acid 1 g in 100 mL saline over 20 minutes must be given within three hours; faster administration causes hypotension.

opts: Congenital heart disease, with a fetal echocardiogram at 22-24 weeks
Duodenal atresia, with serial scans looking for the double bubble
Polycystic kidney disease, with detailed imaging of the renal tract
Unilateral clubfoot, with careful limb views at every subsequent visit
exp: A thickened nuchal translucency with a normal karyotype is an established indication for specialist fetal cardiac assessment.

opts: Only a ventricular septal defect, which is commoner with HELLP syndrome
Only thyroid storm, which complicates severe pre-eclampsia
Only hypertension, which is the hallmark of AFLP rather than HELLP
Pancreatitis, transient diabetes insipidus and renal failure
exp: Pancreatitis, transient diabetes insipidus and renal failure point to acute fatty liver; hypertension and proteinuria point to HELLP.

opts: Monoamniotic twins; parapagus, thoracophagus, rachiphagus and craniophagus
Dichorionic twins, in whom only cephalopagus has ever been described
Monochorionic diamniotic twins, in whom only ischiopagus is described
Dizygotic twins, in whom only parapagus joining has been recorded
exp: Conjoined twins follow splitting after day 13, so they are monoamniotic and monochorionic; the types are named for the shared part.

opts: The head stuck in the occipito-transverse position at the spines despite adequate contractions, usually with an android pelvis
The head arrested at the pelvic brim in the occipito-posterior position
The head arrested at the outlet in the occipito-anterior position
A face presentation arrested in the persistent mento-posterior position
exp: Deep transverse arrest is failure of internal rotation from the transverse position at the level of the ischial spines.

opts: Long forceps with pelvic, cephalic and perineal curves, used for the after-coming head
Short outlet forceps used for a head already on the pelvic floor
Rotational forceps with a sliding lock for a transverse head
Solid-blade forceps designed for a preterm after-coming head
exp: Piper's forceps are long, with a perineal curve, and are applied to the after-coming head while an assistant holds the body up.

opts: Fetal head compression, raising intracranial pressure and causing vagal stimulation
Umbilical vein compression, which reduces venous return to the fetal heart
Uteroplacental insufficiency, which reduces gas exchange at the villi
Placental abruption, which separates the placental bed from the uterus
exp: Early decelerations mirror contractions and are benign; late decelerations come from uteroplacental insufficiency and variable ones from cord compression.

opts: The common peroneal nerve, from prolonged squatting or pressure in the leg supports
The tibial nerve, injured by prolonged positioning in lithotomy
The sciatic nerve, injured by the epidural needle during analgesia
The femoral nerve, compressed by the forceps blades at delivery
exp: Foot drop follows compression of the common peroneal nerve at the fibular neck, classically from squatting or leg supports.

opts: Water intoxication with hyponatraemia when diluted in dextrose, and hypotension if the rate is too fast
Hypertension with hyperkalaemia from a rapid infusion of the drug
Reflex bradycardia with hyperglycaemia from the accompanying dextrose load
High fever with rigors and hypernatraemia from sodium retention
exp: Oxytocin has an antidiuretic effect, so large volumes of 5% dextrose cause hyponatraemia; too rapid a rate causes vasodilatation and hypotension.

opts: Monochorionic worse than dichorionic, and monozygotic worse than dizygotic, apart from cumulative chromosomal risk
Dichorionic twins do worse than monochorionic twins in every respect
Dizygotic twins always do worse than monozygotic twins
All types carry exactly the same risk of fetal complications
exp: Shared circulation drives risk, so monochorionic and monozygotic twins do worse; dizygotic twins carry two independent chromosomal risks instead.

opts: Uterotonic within one minute, delayed cord clamping, controlled cord traction, then intermittent assessment of uterine tone
Cord traction first, then the uterotonic, then clamping, then uterine massage
Early cord clamping, then the uterotonic, then traction, then assessment of tone
Uterine massage first, then the uterotonic, then traction, then late clamping
exp: The four steps run: uterotonic, delayed clamping, controlled cord traction with counter-pressure, then regular assessment of the uterus.

opts: Outpatient, no anaesthesia, terbutaline 0.25 mg subcutaneously, anti-D if Rh-negative, continuous monitoring
An inpatient procedure under general anaesthesia with no tocolysis, followed by induction
In theatre under spinal anaesthesia with nifedipine, always followed by induction
An outpatient procedure under epidural analgesia with no fetal monitoring
exp: Version is done as an outpatient with tocolysis, anti-D cover and continuous monitoring, and without routine anaesthesia or induction.

opts: The gestational sac, a symmetrical fluid collection with an echogenic rim
The secondary yolk sac, which appears before the gestational sac
The embryonic fetal pole, seen as soon as the sac becomes visible
The amniotic membrane, which separates first and outlines the sac
exp: At 4.5-5 weeks the gestational sac is the first structure seen; the yolk sac follows at about 5 weeks and the embryo later.

opts: The placental site, after caesarean section, chorioamnionitis or prolonged rupture of membranes
The cervix, particularly after an operative vaginal delivery at term
The uterine fundus, after a short and uncomplicated labour
The cornua, which are the most exposed areas in a twin pregnancy
exp: Infection begins at the raw placental site; caesarean, chorioamnionitis and prolonged rupture are the principal risk factors.

opts: Tetanic contractions, so it cannot be used before delivery; 0.2 mg intramuscularly, repeated in 2-4 hours
Physiological contractions; 0.5 mg intravenously, stored in clear glass vials
Tetanic contractions; 1 mg orally six-hourly, and requiring refrigeration
Uterine relaxation; 0.2 mg subcutaneously as a single dose
exp: Methylergometrine 0.2 mg intramuscularly gives a sustained tetanic contraction; it is avoided before delivery and given slowly, if at all, intravenously.

opts: Placental alkaline phosphatase and human placental lactogen
Beta-hCG and alpha-fetoprotein, both markedly elevated
CA-125 and inhibin, which closely track the tumour burden
Lactate dehydrogenase and calcitonin, which rise with metastases
exp: Placental site trophoblastic tumour secretes placental alkaline phosphatase and human placental lactogen, with relatively little hCG.

opts: About 10% at the onset of labour falling to about 2% as most rotate; malposition is commoner in nulliparous women
About 2% at the onset rising to about 10%, and commoner in multiparous women throughout
About 25% at the onset falling to about 5%, and commoner in nulliparous women throughout
About 10% throughout labour, with no association with parity at all
exp: Most occipito-posterior heads rotate spontaneously, so the incidence falls from about 10% to about 2%; the malposition is commoner in nulliparas.

opts: Stage 1: the donor bladder is still visible — stage 2: it is not visible, and Doppler is normal in both
Stage 1: the Doppler is already abnormal — stage 2: the Doppler becomes normal again
Stage 2: hydrops fetalis is already present in the recipient twin
Stage 2: one or both twins have already died in utero
exp: Quintero stage 1 still shows a donor bladder; stage 2 loses it, while abnormal Doppler belongs to stage 3 and hydrops to stage 4.

opts: About 85 per cent of cases, which is why it is attempted before hysterectomy
About 50 per cent of cases, so it is rarely worth attempting at all
About 99 per cent of cases, which makes hysterectomy almost unnecessary
About 30 per cent of cases, and only when performed before any drug
exp: Bilateral uterine artery ligation controls bleeding in roughly 85 per cent of cases and preserves fertility, so it precedes hysterectomy.

opts: Repeat caesarean at 36-37 weeks, since contractions become prominent after 37 weeks and raise the rupture risk
A trial of labour aiming for a vaginal birth at 40 completed weeks
A repeat classical section performed at 39 completed weeks
Induction of labour at 38 weeks using prostaglandins
exp: A classical scar ruptures silently and catastrophically, so delivery is planned at 36-37 weeks before strong contractions begin.

opts: Shortens the third stage, reduces blood loss and prevents PPH, but slightly raises the chance of retained placenta
Lengthens the third stage but reduces PPH; the drawback is uterine inversion
Reduces blood loss only, with neonatal anaemia as its drawback
Prevents retained placenta entirely, but at the cost of more PPH
exp: Active management shortens and de-bloods the third stage, at the price of a small increase in retained placenta from early uterotonics.

opts: Huntington's: abdominal traction on the round ligaments — Haultain's: incising the constriction ring — outdated: O'Sullivan and Spinelli
Huntington's: vaginal repair — Haultain's: hydrostatic reduction — outdated: abdominal traction
Huntington's: incising the constriction ring — Haultain's: traction — outdated: embolisation
Huntington's: hydrostatic reduction — Haultain's: the Spinelli repair — outdated: abdominal traction
exp: Huntington's pulls the fundus up with traction on the round ligaments; Haultain's incises the constriction ring from behind; the hydrostatic and Spinelli methods are historical.

opts: Intractable PPH with no plane of cleavage, sometimes with haematuria from bladder invasion
Painless bright-red bleeding at 32 weeks with a soft non-tender uterus
A snowstorm ultrasound appearance with bilateral theca lutein cysts
Fetal distress with a rigid tender uterus and concealed bleeding
exp: Postnatally detected accreta presents as a placenta that cannot be separated, with torrential bleeding and sometimes haematuria.

opts: Handle, finger guard, lock, shank, heel and a fenestrated blade with pelvic and cephalic curves
Cup, chain, handle and hand pump for generating negative pressure
Blade, ratchet, teeth and serrations for gripping the fetal head firmly
Handle, spring and hook for applying traction to the fetal scalp
exp: Each blade has a handle with finger guard, a lock, a shank, a heel and a fenestrated blade with pelvic and cephalic curves.

opts: First-line drug recommended by WHO; 20-40 IU by infusion; avoid a bolus and avoid dextrose
Second-line drug; 10 IU by intravenous bolus, diluted in dextrose
Third-line drug; 5 IU intramuscularly, diluted in whatever fluid is to hand
Not used in postpartum haemorrhage because of the risk of water intoxication
exp: Oxytocin is the WHO first-line uterotonic, given as 20-40 IU by infusion; boluses cause hypotension and dextrose causes hyponatraemia.

opts: Forceps require every prerequisite; vacuum may be used from 6 cm dilatation with an unrotated head
Vacuum requires every prerequisite; forceps may be used from 6 cm dilatation
Both instruments require full cervical dilatation before they can be applied
Forceps may be applied to an unengaged head, but the vacuum may never be
exp: Vacuum extraction is more forgiving: it can be used before full dilatation and does not require the head to be rotated.

opts: Stop at once, turn the baby back to its original position, and proceed to caesarean section
Continue the version quickly so that the procedure can be completed
Give oxytocin and deliver the baby vaginally as soon as possible
Wait thirty minutes for the trace to recover and then try again
exp: Fetal distress during version means abandoning the procedure, reverting the presentation, and delivering by caesarean section.
